daily_reality.summary: Histology technicians (histotechnicians) prepare tissue samples for microscopic examination by pathologists. They work in hospital pathology labs, reference labs, research facilities, and pharmaceutical companies. Standard 40-hour week with possible on-call for frozen sections.
typical_tasks: Processing tissues through fixation, dehydration, and paraffin embedding
Cutting thin tissue sections on microtome (4-6 microns)
Performing routine H&E (hematoxylin and eosin) staining
Performing special stains for specific tissue components
Preparing frozen sections for intraoperative consultation (stat)
Maintaining staining equipment and quality control
Documenting specimen tracking and chain of custody
key_documents: Quality control records for stains and reagents
CAP (College of American Pathologists) inspection checklists

deadlines.routine_processing: 24-48 hours from receipt to slide completion
deadlines.ce_credits: Varies by credential: ASCP HT requires CE for renewal

daily_reality.seasonality: No significant seasonality. Surgical volumes drive workload. Research labs may have grant-cycle-related fluctuations.

regulatory.summary: ASCP Board of Certification (BOC) is the primary credentialing body. Two levels: HT (Histotechnician) and HTL (Histotechnologist). Some states require licensure. CAP accreditation governs laboratory quality standards.

key_laws.name: CLIA '88 (Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments)
key_laws.description: Federal law regulating clinical laboratory quality standards

key_laws.name: CAP (College of American Pathologists) accreditation
key_laws.description: Laboratory accreditation program setting quality standards for histology labs

key_laws.name: State licensure requirements (select states)
key_laws.description: Some states require histology technician licensure (e.g., New York, California, Florida)

key_laws.description: Regulations for handling formaldehyde, xylene, and other histology chemicals

requirements: Associate's degree minimum (HT) or bachelor's degree (HTL)
Completion of NAACLS-accredited histotechnology program or equivalent experience
ASCP BOC certification: HT(ASCP) or HTL(ASCP)
HT route: 1 year clinical experience or 9-month structured program with 480+ clinical hours

regulatory.recent_changes: Growing demand for IHC and molecular pathology skills. ASCP updating competency requirements. Digital pathology integration changing workflow expectations.

Transition to digital pathology requiring new skills

terminology.summary: Pathology laboratory terminology combining tissue processing, staining chemistry, and microscopy language.

terms.H&E: Hematoxylin and eosin — routine tissue stain
terms.IHC: Immunohistochemistry — antibody-based tissue staining for specific proteins
terms.microtomy: Process of cutting thin tissue sections on a microtome
terms.embedding: Process of infiltrating tissue with paraffin wax for sectioning
terms.fixation: Preserving tissue (typically in formalin) to prevent decomposition
terms.frozen section: Rapid tissue preparation for intraoperative diagnosis (10-20 minutes)
terms.cassette: Plastic container holding tissue during processing and embedding
terms.ribbon: Continuous strip of thin tissue sections from microtome
terms.special stains: Non-routine stains highlighting specific tissue components (PAS, trichrome, AFB)
terms.deparaffinize: Removing paraffin from tissue sections before staining
terms.xylene: Chemical solvent used in tissue processing (being replaced by safer alternatives)
terms.formalin: Formaldehyde solution (10% neutral buffered) used for tissue fixation
terms.FFPE: Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded — standard tissue preservation method
terms.grossing: Macroscopic examination and dissection of surgical specimens
terms.CAP: College of American Pathologists — lab accreditation body

career_psychology.summary: Niche laboratory career with moderate salary ($57K-$80K). Growing demand from cancer diagnostics and precision medicine. Shortage of qualified techs creating opportunities. Rewarding for detail-oriented individuals who enjoy lab work.
career_path: Associate's degree in histotechnology (NAACLS-accredited) or related science + clinical experience
Entry-level histotechnician in hospital or reference lab
Specialization: IHC, molecular, frozen sections, research
Lab manager, quality assurance, or educator
fears: Staff shortages increasing pressure and overtime
Automation reducing need for manual skills
Missing critical tissue in frozen section
motivation: Contributing to medical research and advances
burnout_factors: High workload due to staffing shortages
Limited career advancement in small labs

market.summary: Growing demand driven by cancer diagnostics, precision medicine, and IHC/molecular pathology. Staffing shortages creating travel and premium pay opportunities. Digital pathology expanding the field.

demand_forecast.driver: Cancer diagnostics, precision medicine, aging population
demand_forecast.shortage: Significant staffing shortages in histology labs nationwide

Digital pathology (whole slide imaging) changing workflows
Automation of routine processing and staining
Precision medicine increasing demand for specialized tissue testing
Xylene-free and formaldehyde-free alternatives being adopted
